description:
A lightweight Java IDE with on-demand tools and services

Why Lithe
Codex, Claude Code, and other AI coding tools can now handle much of the implementation work. Developers still need an IDE to understand the generated code, follow symbols, run and debug the project, and review every diff. Keeping a heavyweight development environment open for those tasks can mean several gigabytes of resident memory.

Meet Lithe
Lithe is a lightweight IntelliJ IDEA alternative built first for Java and Spring Boot developers. It keeps the core workflows for browsing, editing, navigation, search, Maven, run and debug, Git diff review, local history, and databases.
The Lithe application typically uses about 300–400 MB of baseline memory after opening a regular project. Language servers, terminals, build tools, debuggers, and database helpers start on demand. Actual usage varies with the project and active services.
AI writes the code. Lithe helps you understand it, run it, and review it.

Core features
1. Built for Spring Boot projects and Java development.
2. Maven management, breakpoint debugging, and custom run configurations.
3. Git management and side-by-side diff review.
4. Double-Shift search and Command + Shift + F project-wide search.
5. Process-free lightweight completion and current-file navigation, with on-demand language servers for richer completion, hover, and semantic navigation.
6. Local snapshot history.
7. Multiple projects open within the app.
8. Multiple files open independently in the same window.
9. AI-generated commit messages with customizable formats.
10. Rich Markdown rendering consistent with Yuque syntax.
11. Local application memory usage monitoring.
12. One-command installation and updates through Homebrew.
13. One-click in-app updates and installation.
14. Automatic project entry-point detection with one-click run support for Spring Boot, Java, Maven, Gradle, npm, Cargo, Go, Python, Make, Docker Compose, Procfile, and shell projects.
15. Per-language service switches so language servers can be enabled or disabled independently to match the machine's resources.
16. Multi-line editor tabs for keeping more files visible in the same workspace.
17. Database connection workspace with multiple database types, connection management, SQL history, table browsing, and database operations.
18. Ongoing bug fixes and user experience improvements.
macOS is the current reference product. Windows is an independent React/Tauri implementation. Both products share deterministic commands and contracts through Rust Core while keeping native UI and platform integrations separate.
This release expands Agent, plugin, and remote file workflows, with improvements to terminals, Git, and keyboard navigation.
Highlights
Changes are grouped below.
✨ New features
- macOS adds a project creation wizard with templates supplied by plugins.
- macOS adds Linux SSH connection management, connection tests, remote folder browsing, and file editing and saving.
- macOS supports multiple Claude and Codex subscription accounts with manual switching.
- Claude connections can use either an official subscription or an API key.
- Agent settings add Codex and Claude Code Hook management for actions around tool execution.
- macOS HTML previews support navigation, zoom, in-page search, printing, and PDF export.
- macOS plugins can provide native interfaces and project templates; SVN is now a separate community plugin.
- Windows adds disk installation, enable/disable controls, settings, and separate web tool windows for declarative plugins.
- Windows adds F4 navigation from the project tree and search results, preserving the focused result location.
⚡ Improvements
- macOS database features move to the Database plugin in Lithe Store, with migration for existing connections and history.
- Agent conversations improve long-history loading and group each turn’s reasoning and tool activity into a collapsed section.
- macOS Agent displays tool-image thumbnails with enlarged previews and shows background-task status.
- macOS improves plans, to-do lists, and background-task presentation in Claude Desktop sessions.
- Agent, skills, global instructions, and MCP settings improve; Windows gains additional conversation and execution-state capabilities.
- macOS separates settings-window dragging from workbench updates and unifies common fields, tree lists, and buttons.
- macOS project trees use natural name sorting, and hidden paths share one pattern list.
- Windows terminals support activity-bar drag docking and improve search shortcuts.
- Shared Chinese and English resources reduce missing translations when switching interface languages.
🛠 Fixes
- Closing projects, quitting, or updating confirms and stops running services to avoid leftover background processes.
- Git pushes use the correct upstream target, and large untracked folders appear as directory summaries.
- Windows fixes added-line colors, file navigation order, and preview-tab behavior in diffs.
- Windows Ctrl+Z prioritizes restoring the cursor position after keyboard navigation.
- Java method-call completion leaves arguments empty instead of inserting unwanted values.
- macOS closes terminal tabs after shell exit and synchronizes themes and terminal-application background colors.
- macOS retains native fullscreen with hidden title bars and keeps plugin details within panel boundaries.
- macOS preserves screenshots from earlier user messages when restoring compacted Claude conversations.
- Fixes Agent message spacing and AI settings ordering.
